summary: Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and sinologist. She earned degrees from the University of Chicago (BA 1968) and Columbia University (MA 1970, 1975). She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and served as Professor of History at the University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia C. Stanley (1933–2003) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She completed her BA at the University of Chicago (1966) and her PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (~1966–1972). She taught at Washington State University, UT Austin, UT El Paso, and the University of Łódź (1976–1978).

Patricia Fister is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who completed her PhD at the University of Kansas in 1983. She held curatorial and teaching posts in the US and Japan, notably serving as Professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2007–2019).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a scholar in sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994), studying under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of Perry Link.

Patrick McAllister is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2004–2011) under Helmut Krasser, Karin Preisendanz, and Ernst Steinkellner. He held researcher positions at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and became a Senior Academy Scientist there in 2022.

Patrick Olivelle is an Indologist who studied at the University of Oxford (BA ~1969–1972) and earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1974) under Ludo Rocher. He held faculty posts at Indiana University Bloomington (1974–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin.

Patrick Pranke is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2012) under Robert E. Buswell Jr.
Patrick Robert Cadell (1871–1961) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the East India Company College and Balliol College, Oxford (~1889–1891).
Patrick Tugwell is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He is a doctoral and graduate student at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2026).

Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a Tibetan Buddhist master and philosopher. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught prominent figures such as Shenphen Nangwa and Minyak Kunzang Sonam.
Paul Althaus (1888–1966) was a German scholar of religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1907–1910) and held an academic post at the University of Rostock (~1920–1925).

Paul Arnold Irzel (1861–1931) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Strasbourg and Munich, and completed his PhD at the University of Leipzig in 1890 under the supervision of Ernst Windisch.

Paul B. Courtright is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He held a post at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and served at Emory University, where he is Professor Emeritus (attested 2026).

Paul B. Donnelly is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Geshe Yeshe Thapkay, Losang Yarphel, and Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Carus (1852–1919) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religion. Educated at Greifswald, Strasbourg, and Tübingen (PhD ~1876), he founded the Open Court Publishing Company and edited The Open Court and The Monist from the late 1880s until 1919.

Paul Copp is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at UMass Amherst and Princeton (PhD attested 2005 under Stephen F. Teiser), he held positions at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago, where he became Associate Professor.

Paul Crowe is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Calgary (1992) and a PhD from the University of British Columbia (2005), and was appointed Associate Professor at Simon Fraser University in 2005.

Paul Dahlke (1865–1928) was a German scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. In 1900, he studied in Ceylon under Hikkaduwe Sri Sumangala Thera, Ñāṇissara Thera, and W. D. C. Wagiswara, and he later founded Das Buddhistische Haus in 1924.

Paul David Devanandan (1901–1962) was a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Nizam College, Presidency University, and Yale (PhD ~1931). He served as professor at United Theological College, Bangalore (1932–1949) and director of the Christian Institute for the Study of Religion and Society (1956).
